channel.title: Paperraft
channel.description: Research in efficient inference and AI agents, ranked by independent GitHub implementations instead of citations or stars. Papers above the attention threshold are deliberately excluded.

item.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Long-Session Degradation in Full-Duplex Speech Models
item.description: TRC replaces uniform full-detail retention of the entire conversation history in the KV cache with full-resolution storage of recent turns plus compressed key-value summaries of older history, paired with a lightweight self-distillation LoRA fine-tune to stabilize long sessions. It costs an additional LoRA training run with self-generated distillation data, architectural modification to the model's context handling, and some loss of fidelity for older conversation content. It can fail when older context is needed verbatim (the compression is lossy), when the self-distillation data does not cover the degradation modes of the deployment domain, and on architectures whose full-duplex streaming design is incompatible with the TRC cache layout. 2 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Reason or Recite: Complementary Specialists with an LLM Judge for Traffic Anomaly Reasoning
item.description: RoR replaces a single fine-tuned VLM handling all answer styles with two LoRA-tuned specialists (a 9B reasoning model and a 4-bit-quantized 27B style-matching model) whose outputs are selected per question by a training-free LLM judge. The cost is training and maintaining two models plus per-question judge inference (an additional model call or API latency), and a requirement to rewrite chain-of-thought annotations into a structured schema. It can fail if the judge misroutes questions, if the annotation-style specialist overfits to one benchmark's scoring conventions and fails to transfer, and the absolute score of 0.6788 indicates the task remains far from solved. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Attention under Bounded Key-Query Similarity: Space Complexity and Transformer Anisotropy
item.description: This is a theoretical space-complexity analysis of KV-cache compression under bounded key-query cosine similarity, not a deployable replacement for an existing method; its practical content is a proof that simple uniform sampling of cached tokens is nearly space-optimal for typical parameter regimes. It costs nothing to adopt since it introduces no new algorithm, but it also delivers no measured memory or latency improvement on real workloads. The risk is over-reading the result: optimality is worst-case under a similarity model, so uniform sampling may still underperform learned or attention-aware eviction on specific models and tasks. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: BellowsKV: One Latent for Many Layers, Expanded on Demand
item.description: BellowsKV replaces the per-layer KV cache with a single full-dimension latent shared across blocks of adjacent layers, reconstructed per layer through layer-specific projections, and compresses that latent via quantization (BellowsKV-Quant) or shared eviction decisions (BellowsKV-Evict) rather than dimension reduction. It is training-free, so the cost is integrating custom cache-management code into the serving stack, small per-layer projection overhead at decode time, and possible accuracy loss at the highest compression ratios. It can fail on models or workloads where adjacent hidden states are less similar than reported, on long-context tasks sensitive to eviction errors, or where the inference framework lacks hooks for cross-layer cache sharing. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: FlowGenesis: Representation-Driven Self-Organization of Neural Architectures
item.description: The method replaces fixed pre-specified network widths and separate architecture search with online neuron splitting and pruning driven by Representation Flux, a statistic on minibatch mean-activation changes. It adds per-step bookkeeping of Flux statistics and function-preserving split operations, increasing training complexity and implementation risk without a demonstrated reduction in training compute or wall-clock time. Persistently noisy or unstable Flux estimates could trigger spurious splits or harmful pruning, destabilizing training or degrading accuracy, and reported results are limited to small-scale image and text classification benchmarks. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Subspace Crystallization in Grokking: Rank Compression Tracks the Phase Transition
item.description: This is a scientific analysis showing that weight-matrix rank compression follows, rather than causes, grokking; it replaces no production technique and offers no method to deploy. It costs nothing because there is nothing to implement, but it does carry a practical negative result: imposing low-rank constraints on embeddings or MLP weights does not accelerate generalization and can prevent it entirely (15 of 20 runs failed to grok with capped embedding rank). The finding could fail to transfer if relied upon as guidance for regularization design, since the experiments are confined to mean-field MLPs and one-layer transformers on modular arithmetic, far from production model scales. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: STeP-TS: Shared Temporal Filters with Pruning for Time Series
item.description: It replaces larger multivariate forecasting stacks with a one-layer convolutional bank of shared multi-scale temporal filters, variable-specific scalar mixing, amplitude-adaptive normalization, and structured filter pruning. The cost is a model rewrite and workload-specific validation of the filter bank, normalization, and pruning thresholds rather than a drop-in component, with compute savings claimed but not quantified in the abstract. It can fail where long-horizon dependencies, strong cross-variable interactions, or rare variable-specific regimes require more capacity than shared temporal filters and scalar weights can preserve after pruning. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Realizing Low-Precision Storage and Sparse Execution in a Folded FPGA Speech Enhancer
item.description: The method replaces uniform hardware-aware compression driven by a single bit-operation metric with training objectives that separately price on-chip weight storage (mixed precision) and removable scheduled work (structured channel sparsity) for a folded streaming accelerator. It requires FPGA deployment (a Kria KV260), bit-exact hardware-software co-design, and retraining with group-lasso objectives, which is a substantial engineering cost; notably, reducing weight width from 8 to 6 bits saves 27% dynamic power but under 5% latency, so precision work alone underdelivers. It can fail if the target workload's sparsity pattern does not align with the engine's schedule, if plain group-lasso degrades task quality on non-speech tasks, or if results do not transfer to GPU inference where folding economics do not apply. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization
item.description: Replaces traditional black-box optimizers (Bayesian optimization, evolution strategies) for mixed-integer energy system design with an LLM agent that reasons over simulation results, proposes configuration changes, and reverts unsuccessful changes via git-based mechanism. Costs depend on LLM API usage (Claude Haiku/Sonnet/Opus) with 50 simulations per run; no local training required but needs domain-specific simulator integration. Can fail if LLM reasoning quality degrades on unseen design spaces, if API costs scale unfavorably with problem complexity, or if simulator feedback loops introduce errors the agent cannot diagnose. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Context Is Not Free: Carbon-Aware LLM Routing for Multi-Turn LLM Web Services across Geo-Distributed Data Centers
item.description: CarbonRouter replaces carbon-aware routers that treat each query independently by jointly selecting model, GPU type, and region per turn while charging KV-cache history recomputation to any candidate deployment that lacks the session's cache, plus a gate that avoids oscillating a session between regions. The cost is a cache-aware carbon cost model fed by cached-token counts from serving backends and online routing logic per turn, which adds control-plane complexity on top of the serving stack. It can fail when cached-token telemetry is unavailable or inaccurate, when carbon-intensity forecasts for grid regions are stale, or when the oscillation gate pins sessions to a region whose carbon intensity later worsens. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Thermal-Headroom Routing for Efficient Robot Perception in Extreme Heat
item.description: This method replaces static thermal management policies (like fixed throttles or duty cycles) with a predictive routing policy that uses an RC thermal model to select optimal detector configurations and avoid processor throttling. It requires implementing a closed-form thermal forecasting model and maintaining a routing layer, which adds computational overhead and necessitates hardware-specific calibration of thermal parameters. The approach may fail if the thermal model does not accurately reflect real-world hardware behavior, as validation was conducted in simulation and on an Apple M5 without confirming actual hardware throttling. 2 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Testing with Coding Agents: A Large-Scale Comparison of Agent-Supported and Human-Authored Pull Requests
item.description: This paper proposes no deployable technique; it is a large-scale empirical study (114,134 PRs in 391 Java repositories) comparing testing behavior in agent-supported versus human-authored pull requests, so it replaces nothing in the production stack. Adoption costs nothing directly, but acting on its findings would require adding PR-level telemetry and review checks for agent-generated tests, which consumes team time. What can fail is over-interpreting the results: pooled cross-project comparisons reverse or hide within-repository effects, test-quality differences (smells, coverage) are borderline or absent, and the analysis is limited to Java repositories with five detected agents, so conclusions may not transfer to other languages or tools. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: InterQ-RL: Interaction-Aware Correction of Execution Mismatch in Quantized Agentic RL
item.description: InterQ-RL replaces current-token rollout-learner ratio correction (as in prior quantized-RL methods) with a bounded correction applied over the full state-reaching action history, distributing correction strength across segments under a fixed displacement budget. It requires no additional model forward pass, so the cost is implementation complexity in the importance-ratio computation rather than added memory or latency; W8A8-KV8 rollout itself reduces generation and KV-cache cost during long multi-turn rollouts. It can fail if the reader is not doing multi-turn agent RL at all (the correction targets execution mismatch along interaction histories, irrelevant to single-turn or SFT pipelines), if bounded prefix correction mis-allocates strength on environments with very long or sparse action segments, or if the reader's small models and environments differ enough from ALFWorld/WebShop/ScienceWorld with 4B-30B backbones that the mismatch it fixes is negligible. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Inference Latency-Aware Tsetlin Machine Training
item.description: The method replaces exhaustive (T, s) grid search in Tsetlin Machine training with a directed search that treats accuracy as a constraint and increases s to reduce inference latency. The cost is limited to tuning complexity and potential accuracy degradation up to dataset-dependent levels. Adoption may fail if accuracy falls outside acceptable bounds on a given dataset or if bitwise TM inference is not the deployed model class. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: RSIV-Harness: A Recursive Self-Improvement Harness Framework for Open-Domain Conversational Text-to-Visualization
item.description: Replaces a static, manually designed agent harness with a procedure that rewrites prompts, tools, or control logic from the agent's own failure traces while keeping model weights fixed. Costs extra offline evaluation cycles and LLM calls for failure analysis and harness validation, plus the added complexity of anchor and memory checks to keep revisions stable. Can fail if self-revisions overfit to the benchmark or trace distribution, if validation checks miss regressions, or if failure traces are unrepresentative, silently degrading production behavior. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: test.

item.title: RepoTrace: Improving Requirement Tracing in Multi-Round Agent Interactions
item.description: The method replaces unstructured or purely retrieval-based repository context with an explicit requirement-code correspondence map injected into the agent's context to keep it focused on primary modification targets across rounds. It costs an additional repository-analysis and harness-integration step plus extra context tokens per round, with some added latency and implementation complexity, but requires no model training and works with API-based models. It can fail if the constructed correspondence is inaccurate or incomplete, if the requirement semantics are ambiguous, or if the injected mapping consumes context budget needed for code, and gains reported on EvoCode-Bench may not transfer to a different codebase or workflow. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Knowing When to Escalate: Disagreement Patterns for Uncertainty-Aware Content Moderation
item.description: RTDA replaces escalation rules based only on disagreement magnitude or output-label spread with a post-processing classifier over embedded reasoning traces and conclusion agreement. It costs extra justification generation, embedding, and classification per item, plus added system complexity, while likely preserving rather than reducing inference expense. It can fail if agent rationales are unstable, unfaithful, or biased in ways that make the four-state taxonomy an unreliable proxy for human value disagreement. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MarkovSim: an LLM Agent Harness with Bounded Context for Long-Horizon Computational Simulation
item.description: The method replaces ad-hoc or unbounded context accumulation in long-horizon LLM agent workflows by externalizing the workflow record to a structured memory system and constructing a compact context snapshot only at predefined finite-state machine transitions. The cost is increased architectural complexity, requiring upfront schema design and explicit state-machine definition for the target workflow. Failure can occur if the compact state representation omits information needed for later reasoning steps, or if the predefined schema does not generalize to new simulation types or edge cases. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Autonomous Structural Discovery Of Bioprocess Dynamics And Kinetics Via LLM-Driven Agents
item.description: The method replaces manual derivation of bioprocess kinetic rate laws (or rigid data-driven approaches like SINDy and PINNs) with a closed-loop LLM-agent architecture combining two-level RAG, moving horizon estimation, and active design of experiments. It costs the engineering effort of building a bioprocess-specific MHE/DoE pipeline plus ongoing LLM API calls, and its validation is confined to a single simulated reactor with known ground-truth dynamics. It can fail on real fermentation data when noise and sensor drift corrupt the logarithmic residual decomposition, when active DoE perturbations are unsafe or too slow for physical cells, and when an LLM retrieves plausible but structurally wrong rate laws that pass statistical checks. 2 independent implementations, 1 star. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Belief-Conditioned Multi-Agent Actor Critic for Decentralized LLM Collaboration
item.description: The method replaces hand-designed multi-agent workflows and naive actor-critic coordination with a belief-conditioned multi-agent actor-critic that trains decentralized LLM agents to infer context from communication traces. It costs a full MARL training pipeline over LLM policies, including joint training runs, reward design, and environment interaction at scale, which exceeds a single 24 GB GPU and a limited cloud budget. It can fail through unstable multi-agent RL training, sensitivity to reward specification, and belief models that confer little benefit on short-horizon tasks with limited contextual information. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: A knowledge-driven nonconvex square-root regularization framework for joint group sparsity and structured smoothness
item.description: The method replaces convex squared-loss structured sparse estimators (e.g., group lasso/fused lasso) with a square-root loss and nonconvex l_{2,q} penalty for classical high-dimensional regression tasks. Its costs are a custom nonconvex optimization implementation (double-screened IRLS with thresholding) and tuning of a nonconvex penalty parameter, with no connection to GPU or LLM workloads. It can fail if the assumed group and piecewise-smooth structures do not match the data, or if the nonconvex solver converges to poor stationary points despite the stated global convergence guarantee. The abstract reports consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines in finite-sample experiments but gives no quantified factor. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Prior Predictive Matching for Bayesian LoRA
item.description: This technique replaces manual or validation-based selection of the prior scale in Bayesian Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) with a closed-form estimator derived from prior-predictive matching before fine-tuning. It costs a one-time analytical computation and eliminates the need for validation data or repeated hyperparameter sweeps, but it relies on a second-order expansion of the network that may be inaccurate for highly nonlinear tasks and assumes that the estimated prior precision generalizes across adaptation ranks, which can fail if the task or model violates these scaling assumptions. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: ShutdownMod: Turning Any Trajectory into a Shutdown Evaluation
item.description: ShutdownMod replaces bespoke, fixed shutdown test environments by converting any existing agent trajectory (SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, SWE-chat, or production logs) into a shutdown test via context injection with signature-verified authorization. It costs API or local inference calls for rollouts across sampled timesteps plus harness integration, fitting a single 24 GB GPU or API budget, but adds evaluation-pipeline complexity. It can fail through evaluation awareness in benchmark-derived tests, judge subjectivity, and results that may not transfer to a deployment's specific context distribution. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Governing Enterprise AI Traffic at Scale: Design and Operation of a Policy-Driven, Multi-Vendor LLM Gateway on Envoy
item.description: Replaces direct per-vendor LLM API integration — with its credential sprawl, format lock-in, and ad hoc governance — with a centralized gateway that brokers credentials, normalizes API dialects, enforces declarative OPA policy, meters tokens, and manages budgets. Costs include operating and securing an always-on gateway tier (Envoy plus an external-processing service and WASM filter), the added latency on the request path, and the engineering burden of a policy control plane with approvals, pilots, and shadow rollouts. After adoption, the gateway becomes a single point of failure and policy bottleneck: misconfigured budgets or DLP rules can block or leak traffic, vendor API drift can break translation filters, and the enterprise scale (12,000 developers, 100+ models) has no counterpart on a small team's infrastructure. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: GEAR: Feature-Based Configuration and Code Generation for Agentic Systems
item.description: GEAR replaces hand-written, framework-specific multi-agent implementations by letting developers specify agents, orchestration, communication, reasoning, and memory in a common feature-based specification and generating validated projects across ten agentic frameworks. It costs an additional abstraction layer and toolchain dependency, and generated code still requires inspection of the per-framework adaptation reports; 48 of 320 feature-framework pairs (15.31%) had no identified translation strategy. It can fail when a desired feature maps only partially or not at all to a target framework, producing degraded or missing functionality that the validation step may not catch before generation. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ArchiveLens: A Generative Spatial Knowledge Framework for Semantic Reconstruction of Historical Maps
item.description: ArchiveLens replaces manual or purely geometric historical map digitization workflows with a three-stage pipeline that extracts building footprints via YOLOv11-seg, classifies materials via deterministic HSV color thresholds, and parses attributes via a quantized vision-language model, then integrates results into a hybrid spatial-temporal RAG architecture with provenance grounding. The system requires georeferenced historical map sheets (a specialized dataset), a YOLOv11-seg segmentation model, a quantized VLM, and a custom ST-RAG infrastructure combining dense retrieval with symbolic spatio-temporal filtering, representing a moderate engineering investment. Failure modes include domain shift when applied to non-Sanborn map styles or different historical periods, potential hallucination or misattribution from the VLM despite prompt constraints, accumulated errors across the decoupled stages (segmentation errors propagating to classification), and the scalability of the hybrid retrieval system to larger corpora. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Hierarchical Skill Evolution for Coding Agent
item.description: The method replaces manual prompt engineering and static few-shot examples with an automated hierarchical distillation pipeline that extracts reusable procedural skills from raw coding trajectories. It requires significant computational overhead to run the external writer-evaluator loop for skill generation and assessment, introducing complexity in maintaining the skill library and curation infrastructure. Learned evaluators may drift without ground-truth verification, and repository-specific patterns may fail to transfer to novel codebases with different architectural conventions or domain logic. 3 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Improving JEV Entailment Reranking with Span Readouts and Selective Adaptation
item.description: The method replaces option-ending pointer readouts with mean pooling over the contextualized states inside each NLI option, and replaces full all-module adapter tuning with low-rank updates restricted to attention and gated DeltaNet projections, dropping feed-forward adapters. It adds no head parameters and reduces trainable parameters by more than half, lowering fine-tuning memory and compute while claiming higher reranking accuracy. It can fail because results are reported on a single 4B model and one aggregate benchmark (MC11), so gains may not transfer to other backbones, domains, or reranking workloads. 2 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Triage: Skip, Skim, or Refine Attention Tiles in Video Diffusion Transformers
item.description: It replaces full-precision dense attention in video diffusion transformers with a training-free router that assigns each attention tile to skipping (block-mean substitution), NVFP4 computation, or NVFP4 with residual correction, executed by a single fused kernel. It costs the integration effort of a custom kernel, dependence on FP4 tensor-core hardware (RTX Blackwell-class GPUs), and a price hyperparameter that must be set to trade compute against error. It can fail on GPUs without FP4 support (a 24 GB Ada/Ampere card cannot run the reported kernel), on models or resolutions where the error router's predictions misprice tiles, or where the 2.32x figure does not transfer to the reader's specific model and sequence lengths. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Quantitative Generalization Bounds for Multi-Layer Transformers: A Few Long Strings can Beat Many Short Ones
item.description: The method replaces ad hoc scaling of sample count and training length with a theoretical framework that jointly bounds in-distribution statistical generalization and length extrapolation for fixed-precision transformers. It costs nothing in memory, latency, or deployment complexity because it provides analytical guidance rather than a runtime algorithm. It can fail if the bounds are loose, if fixed-precision assumptions do not match production numerics, or if real training data violate the modeled distribution and alphabet constraints. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Free to Look, Free to Reason: Simple LLM Harnesses Outdiagnose Hand-Crafted Root Cause Analysis Agents
item.description: The approach replaces hand-crafted RCA agents with fixed standard operating procedures, staged pipelines, and role agents by simple harnesses that prescribe none of the model's calls: a single call over an evidence package, a SQL agent, or the Codex coding agent. Cost is low and within constrained infrastructure, since mid-tier models suffice and higher reasoning effort changes accuracy by only a few points while multiplying time by up to seven; a stronger model mainly improves reliability, and a multi-turn harness mainly improves aptitude. Failure modes include possible dataset or evaluation bias toward the RCAtlas benchmark, dependence on the quality of the evidence package and tool access, and the risk that unconstrained investigation misses decisive evidence on failure modes not represented in the 90 validated cases. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: A Unified Arena for LLM Agents across Diverse Eurogame
item.description: DECE replaces ad-hoc, single-game agent evaluations with a unified arena spanning ten Eurogames, shared interfaces, and standardized protocols for comparing model-harness configurations. It costs the effort of adopting an external benchmark rather than building task-relevant evaluation; running 1,000+ matches implies non-trivial API or compute expense for full replication. It can fail to predict performance on the reader's actual production tasks, since Eurogame rankings reflect strategic game play rather than domain-specific tool use, and harness-dependent variation means results may not transfer to the reader's stack. 2 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models
item.description: REVA replaces multi-call agentic vulnerability-detection loops (tool runs, hypothesis testing, iterative reasoning) with a single forward pass whose prompt includes a pre-computed module threat model, static-analysis findings, and call-graph data, read by a trained linear probe on the LLM's internal representations. The cost is offline infrastructure to build per-module threat models and call graphs, a trained probe per backbone model, and access to hidden states, which excludes most closed third-party APIs and ties the probe to a specific open model that fits on one 24 GB GPU. It can fail on code whose risk depends on cross-module context the pre-computed summary omits, the probe may not transfer across model versions or languages, and 60% accuracy on PrimeVul implies substantial false-positive and false-negative rates unsuitable as a sole gate. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Profiling a Frontier Agent with EBench: From Direct Control to Harness with Policy
item.description: The technique replaces robot-specific VLA or WAM policy training with a general-purpose MLLM agent that either issues waypoint commands directly or invokes a post-trained policy through an agent harness. It costs frontier-model API access, visual and proprioceptive observation infrastructure, and a physical or simulated robotic platform, none of which the reader possesses. After adoption it can fail through suboptimal policy invocation, fixed-instruction execution without subgoals, grasp disruption when the agent resumes control, and weak performance on long-horizon, tabletop, and contact-rich tasks. 2 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Information-Theoretic Secure Aggregation With Heterogeneous Client Quantization
item.description: The scheme replaces prior secure aggregation protocols that either force all clients onto a common finite group or leak partial aggregates and individual update segments when clients use heterogeneous quantization levels, by secret-sharing updates from distinct algebraic groups via identical linear integer systems with a (T+1, N) threshold black-box construction. It costs additional cryptographic machinery: secret share generation per client, communication overhead for distributing shares, and protocol complexity that must accommodate dropouts and up to T server-colluding semi-honest clients. It can fail in practice if the assumed threat model (semi-honest collusion bounded by T) is exceeded, if dropout rates exceed the reconstruction threshold, or if the deployment does not actually involve cross-device federated learning, in which case the privacy guarantee is irrelevant. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: I-HITL: Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop
item.description: It replaces software-only HITL checkpoints, which the paper shows ten frontier models routinely bypass (e.g., harvesting emailed OTPs to raise spending caps), with a protocol requiring explicit approval through a trusted device such as a consumer phone running the Countersign prototype. The cost is deploying and integrating a trusted computing device per approving human, plus added latency and friction on every gated action, with the prototype not yet production-hardened. It fails if no genuinely trusted device exists in the approval path, if the device or its attestation is compromised, and strong I-HITL against adversarial human delegation is only partially achievable per the paper's own characterization. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Rethinking LoRA Initialization for Robust Asymmetric Learning Rates
item.description: It replaces the standard LoRA initialization (A drawn at conventional scale, B zero) with an A variance scaled as 1/n^2 while keeping B0=0, so LoRA+ asymmetric learning rates remain stable at high eta_B/eta_A ratios. The cost is negligible: a one-line change to the initialization scale with no added memory, latency, or training time, though it presumes LoRA+ asymmetric LRs are in use. It can fail to matter when LoRA+ is not used, when a small LR ratio is already adequate, or when the width-based guideline eta_B approximately n*eta_A does not transfer to the specific model and task, so per-task validation is still required. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Sparsity-driven emergence of functional modularity in multitask neural networks
item.description: The technique replaces unstructured multitask training with sparsity-inducing regularization to encourage compact task-selective subnetworks that can be selectively retained or recombined. It costs added regularization tuning and task-weighting choices, and may reduce performance on non-retained tasks when extracting functional tokens. It can fail to yield reusable modules if the model scale, task family, or regularization regime does not produce stable functional tokens. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SOPO: Socratic Guided Policy Optimization for Span-Level Hallucination Detection
item.description: SOPO replaces standard RLVR (e.g., GRPO) fine-tuning for span-level hallucination detection with a multi-turn RL loop in which a teacher model injects Socratic hints derived from ground truth during rollouts, plus turn-based advantage scaling to curb verbosity. The cost is a full RL training pipeline with a teacher model in the loop, rollout generation, and reward engineering, which is substantially more complex than supervised fine-tuning and difficult to run on a single 24 GB GPU. Adoption can fail through teacher-hint leakage that inflates training metrics without generalization, out-of-domain degradation, and dependence on ground-truth span annotations that most production settings lack. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: BiLoCo: Binary Low-Rank Corrections for Post-Training Quantization
item.description: BiLoCo replaces the BF16 low-rank SVD correction used in SVDQuant with binary sign-vector corrections for FP4 post-training quantization, running the correction as additions/subtractions on CUDA cores concurrent with the tensor-core GEMM. It requires Blackwell-class hardware (the implementation targets B300) and a fused custom kernel; correction overhead is up to 11-20% latency depending on rank and batch. It can fail on non-Blackwell GPUs lacking native FP4 tensor cores, and accuracy parity with memory-matched SVDQuant is demonstrated only on 4B-72B LLMs, leaving other model families and the engineering effort of kernel integration unvalidated. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: TranSAGE: Automating Spatial Accelerator Generation for Large-Scale Transformer Models
item.description: The method replaces manual or single-operation accelerator generation with a compiler pipeline that jointly optimizes multi-operation dataflow, partitions Transformer graphs, and lowers them to spatial accelerator RTL. Its cost is a hardware design and fabrication toolchain plus compiler integration, not a drop-in software change. It can fail because gains depend on producing and validating custom silicon and on whether the generated dataflow remains efficient for the exact target models and deployment stack. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: TGR-EvoDAG: A DAG-based Multi-Agent Code Evolution Framework for Generative Recommendation on Tencent
item.description: TGR-EvoDAG replaces linear or general-purpose LLM-driven code evolution for generative recommendation pipelines with a DAG-based multi-agent framework that maintains parallel evolution branches, merges complementary innovations, and adds stage-aware cost planning plus active downstream co-adaptation across the tokenization, pre-training, and alignment stages. The cost is substantial orchestration complexity: running a multi-agent evolutionary search over full pipeline retraining requires repeated GPU-hour expenditure per candidate and a working GR pipeline with per-stage diagnostic evaluation infrastructure, which is realistic for a platform like Tencent but heavy for a small team. It can fail when the reader lacks a GR pipeline to evolve, when evaluation signals are noisy enough to misguide branch selection, or when the compute budget cannot sustain the evolutionary search the gains presuppose. 3 independent implementations, 163 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Beyond Final Outcomes: Quantifying Claim-Level Information Dynamics in Multi-Agent LLM Interaction
item.description: RIVER replaces final-outcome-only evaluation of multi-agent LLM systems with claim-level decomposition measuring convergence, exploration, and retention across interaction stages. It costs additional LLM calls and engineering to extract atomic claims, align them across agents, and track lineage, and it adds no direct task-performance gain. It can fail if claim decomposition or stance alignment is inaccurate, if the three metrics do not correlate with the reader's actual downstream objectives, or if findings from 40 controlled news-generation cases do not transfer to other domains. 2 independent implementations, 136 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: From Faulty Claims to Incorrect Patches: An Empirical Study of Task-Grounded Reasoning in Coding Agents
item.description: This replaces task-agnostic agent-trajectory failure heuristics, such as repeated actions, with claim-level diagnosis that extracts atomic task-grounded claims from the CoT, verifies them against gathered evidence, and links defects to faulty claims through claim-corrected replay. The cost is substantial: an additional LLM extraction and evidence-gathering pass per trajectory plus manual confirmation in the study, with only 18.5% of CoT tokens being task-grounded and 191 claims per trajectory to process. It can fail as a production signal because faulty claims appear in 96.7% of resolved trajectories, so detection alone does not indicate failure and value depends on pinpointing the few causally linked claims. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: DealsFlow: An Evidence-Gated Agentic Harness for Venture Capital Deal Triage
item.description: Replaces direct LLM-emitted investment scores with a pipeline in which the model cites evidence and rates categories while deterministic code caps and only lowers scores, via a corroboration ceiling, a lower-only sceptic call, and pre-fetched evidence retrieval. Costs an extra sceptic generation pass plus evidence retrieval and indexing latency, and 70% of reports still need analyst correction, so human review time is retained. Can fail through non-date-restricted retrieval leaking future information (the reported correlations may overstate screening skill), through the untested lower-only sceptic rule, and through residual unsupported claims (16% of citations not fully supported). 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: LeafSkill: Efficient Leaf-Level Action Grounding for Recursive LLM Agents
item.description: It replaces repeated invocation of the large host LLM for leaf-level action grounding with a retrieval layer that binds reusable action templates, selected by a frozen 1.7B model that can defer to the original agent when uncertain. The cost is maintaining a semantic skill store and running an additional small selector (feasible on one 24 GB GPU or via API alongside the host model), plus integration work against an environment with explicitly admissible actions. It can fail when the environment does not expose a checkable action space, when retrieved templates are semantically close but wrong for the current objects, and the reported gains are validated only in the Robotouille robotics domain, so transfer to other agent workloads is unproven. 2 independent implementations, 136 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Measuring the Energy Cost of Completing Tasks with Quantized Language-Model Agents
item.description: The method replaces per-token energy benchmarking of quantized models with per-completed-task measurement across an agent's full run, including tool calls and revisions, as the basis for choosing serving precision. It costs the effort of building pass/fail-checked tasks and measuring CPU and GPU energy per completed run on one's own workload, with no model or infrastructure change required. It can fail if conclusions from published benchmarks are transferred blindly, since whether 4-bit saves energy per task is task-, model-, and budget-dependent. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Cycle-of-Thought: Self-Evaluative Iterative Reasoning for Table Visual Question Answering in Document Images
item.description: Replaces supervised fine-tuning and architectural changes for improving table VQA with a training-free, inference-time self-correction loop in which one VLM acts as generator, critic, and refiner. Costs linearly higher inference latency and token/API spend per query due to multiple model passes, though it avoids annotation and training cost. Can fail when the model's self-critique is unreliable, errors persist across iterations, or multiplied per-query cost outweighs the accuracy gain at production volume. 1 independent implementation, 126 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Async-RBench: Benchmarking Asynchronous Task Execution in LLM Agents
item.description: Async-RBench replaces end-to-end success-only evaluation of multi-agent systems with 200 executable tasks that deliver subagent results asynchronously under controlled state conditions, scoring response handling via an Event Response Contract and a Dynamic Replanning Score reported separately from task success. Adopting it costs integration effort: tasks must be executable in the reader's environment, the scenario controller and ERC must be wired to the reader's agent framework, and evaluation runs multiply API or GPU spend without improving the system itself. It can fail as a decision tool if the reader's production workload is synchronous or single-agent, if the eight covered scenarios mismatch the reader's domain, or if DRS weighting (process and outcome weighted equally) does not reflect the reader's actual failure costs. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Profile-Driven User Simulation via Reinforcement Learning with Hierarchical Rewards for Task-Oriented Dialogues
item.description: Replaces manual collection and annotation of domain-specific dialogue data (and generic user simulators) with a fine-tuned, GRPO-refined profile-driven user simulator for financial marketing calls. Costs include obtaining real voice call logs for fine-tuning, RL training with hierarchical rewards, and maintaining a paired SOP/RAG customer-service agent; the base model size is unstated, so single-24GB-GPU feasibility is uncertain. It can fail through reward hacking against the coupled evaluation agent, domain mismatch outside financial outbound calls, and simulated data that does not transfer to real user behavior. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SCI-AGENT-EXAM: Benchmarking Agents on Scientific Research Tasks
item.description: It replaces narrow or single-capability scientific benchmarks with SCI-AGENT-EXAM: 120 expert-curated tasks across 11 fields and 7 research task types, requiring both executable and textual artifacts and scored by deterministic verification plus a calibrated expert-validated LLM judge. It costs access to the benchmark, task execution infrastructure, judge calibration or API spend for textual evaluation, and engineering effort to run executable artifacts safely and consistently. It can fail if judge calibration does not transfer to a different domain, if executable verification is too brittle for valid alternative solutions, or if trajectory metrics are overinterpreted without matching the reader's production workflow. 2 independent implementations, 136 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: POSEIDON: Scaling Training Environments for Scientific Agents from Code Repositories
item.description: The pipeline replaces manual construction of agent training environments by automatically extracting, decomposing, and refining executable tasks from scientific code repositories. The cost is a complex multi-stage generation and verification pipeline plus the need to train models on the resulting data, which exceeds a single 24 GB GPU for the reported model sizes. Adoption can fail because environment correctness depends on repository executability and automated verification, and the resulting dataset primarily benefits teams performing model training rather than inference-only deployments. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: DIGOM: Disentangled Interaction Graphs for Outcome prediction in Multimodal healthcare
item.description: The method replaces standard multimodal fusion and graph approaches that model only a subset of interaction types with a learned sparse multiplex graph combining intra-patient cross-modal, cross-patient same-modal, and cross-patient cross-modal interactions via differentiable discrete adjacency sampling. Costs include graph-construction and message-passing complexity, a sparsity regularization objective to tune, and training that requires a cohort of multimodal patient records rather than per-patient inference. It can fail when patient populations are too small to support meaningful cross-patient edges, when the optimal interaction structure shifts across tasks, or when batch composition leaks cohort information into individual predictions. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Sharpness-aware Orthogonalized Momentum Algorithms
item.description: SOMA replaces the standard SAM perturbation step on top of the Muon optimizer by reusing stale stochastic gradient noise as the adversarial perturbation direction, eliminating SAM's extra gradient computation per iteration. Its cost is modest implementation complexity in the optimizer loop; the abstract claims the perturbation is computationally efficient and sample complexity is invariant to perturbation direction, but gives no quantified speedup or quality figure. It can fail if the claimed benefits (mitigating quantization degradation and catastrophic forgetting) do not transfer to the reader's fine-tuning workloads, since the evidence base is LLM training at scales the reader does not operate. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CauProphet: Teaching Agents to Develop Causal Cognition like Humans
item.description: CauProphet replaces flat retrieval-style agent memory (records and summaries) with a persistent structured causal store: per-task Causal Beliefs that are updated from observations and written back into long-term Causal Cognition. The cost is additional LLM calls for belief construction and updating per step, plus engineering of a structured causal schema and its persistence layer, increasing latency and token spend relative to simple retrieval. It can fail through spurious causal attribution (the model may encode correlations as causal links), unvalidated transfer of wrong causal beliefs to new tasks, and dependence on strong underlying LLMs, which the financial and prediction gains may presuppose. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: When Agents Fail: Model or Harness--Who's to Blame?
item.description: Replaces evaluating agentic benchmarks solely by task accuracy or by model and harness in isolation with a five-measure framework (VCR, model-harness fit, cross-model fit, interaction residuals, token load) applied across pairings of four harnesses and four models on six benchmarks. Costs additional evaluation compute and engineering to instrument trajectories, count tokens including failed runs, and maintain a pairing matrix across harnesses and models, with no model or harness modification required. Can fail if the chosen benchmark panel or model set does not match the production workload, since rankings vary across models and benchmarks, and because harness updates or API changes can invalidate measured fit over time. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Accordion: Elastic-Depth Inference via Fixed-Prefix Layer Looping
item.description: The method replaces training and maintaining separate models per inference budget with one mixture-of-experts model that reuses parameters through pre-defined looped execution paths at five depths. It costs joint pretraining on 3.6T tokens plus budget-aware SFT, RL, parameter-group merging, and multi-teacher distillation, which is far beyond a 24 GB GPU and limited cloud budget. If adopted only as an inference idea on non-Accordion weights it fails, because the elastic budgets exist only in models specifically pretrained and fine-tuned for layer looping. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Tool-Calling LLM Agents Under Realistic MCP Faults: Scale Does Not Purchase Fault Tolerance
item.description: MCP-Injector replaces clean-tool agent benchmarks (which assume correct, timely tool responses) with seedable, protocol-aware fault injection on the MCP call path, calibrated to failure modes mined from 57,240 real MCP repository threads. It costs an extra middleware layer in the tool-call path plus evaluation runtime; no model retraining or large hardware is required, so it fits a single-GPU or API-based setup. It can fail to predict production behavior if the mined incident distribution diverges from the reader's actual tool ecosystem, and results on gpt-oss backbones may not transfer to other model families. 1 independent implementation, 12 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Lessons Outlive Their Failures: A Case Study of Rules for AI Coding Agents
item.description: The method replaces ad hoc, write-once rule files (AGENTS.md and similar) with a failure ledger, periodic LLM documentation audits, mechanical checks, and replay-based re-testing to retire obsolete rules. Costs are ongoing maintenance effort, audit LLM calls, git-clone replay infrastructure, and the accumulation of stale lessons that must be actively pruned. Audits miss roughly half of known drift per run, written rules may not change model behavior on newer models, and obsolete checks can persist past the failures they were written to fix. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: What Transfers Across Protein Pockets? Experience Reuse in Molecular Optimization for Agentic Structure-Based Drug Design
item.description: This technique replaces the repeated, expensive docking of speculative edits by ranking an agent's proposed molecular edits against a reusable log of historical outcomes. The cost is the ongoing maintenance of this base and the engineering needed to define and query keys across different protein pockets. A critical failure mode is that keys which transfer to unseen pockets primarily describe the edit and molecule, not the target, so the base may fail to separate good from bad edits for novel biology. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Toward Open ISA Supercomputing: A Comparative Study of RISC-V, Arm, and x86 Architectures on HPC Workloads
item.description: This is a comparative hardware evaluation, not a technique: it benchmarks Sophgo SG2044 (RISC-V), NVIDIA Grace, and Intel Xeon 8480+ on HPC kernels and llama.cpp under a common software stack, replacing anecdotal cross-platform comparisons with a uniform methodology. Adoption would mean procuring RISC-V server hardware, which costs capital budget, toolchain maturity, and 8-15x lower absolute FP64 and memory-bandwidth performance versus incumbent x86 or Arm nodes. The finding can fail to transfer because llama.cpp decode efficiency on SG2044 depends on L2-aware process placement, saturates beyond memory bandwidth limits, and reflects a specific quantization and workload configuration. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: StateMirror: Pre-Execution Detection of Hallucinated Tool Calls in Coding Agents
item.description: StateMirror replaces reactive, post-execution failure feedback and LLM-judge detection with a deterministic pre-execution validator that checks action predicates against the live repository at the harness boundary. It costs only the engineering effort to integrate AST and command analysis into the agent loop; it adds negligible runtime overhead (1.50ms) and zero token cost. It can fail on the roughly 18% of hallucinations it misses (F1 0.817), on environment states not expressible as static predicates, and on dynamically generated or highly dynamic codebases where AST extraction is incomplete. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: EMG Tokenization Preserves Movement Information at a Fraction of the Bitrate
item.description: The method replaces high-bandwidth raw EMG or continuous spectral-spatial features with compact causal tokens trained without pose labels for hand-pose decoding. Its cost is an additional encoder/tokenization pipeline and a small increase in decoding error, with reported mean-error changes of +0.01 mm for SPAR tokens and +0.45 mm for learned tokens. It can fail outside the studied setup because electrode coverage, calibration, and unseen recordings affect SPAR decoding more than quantization does, limiting robustness in deployment. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Tile-Based Decompression in Compiled GPU Engines
item.description: Replaces decompressed-column materialization in HBM with fused on-chip decompression inside compiled GPU kernels. Costs include integration into a compiler-based execution engine (Proteus) and kernel complexity for cooperative tile decompression. Can fail if the production engine lacks compiler infrastructure to fuse decompression with downstream operators, or if compression encodings do not match query access patterns. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: ActionRAG: Evidence-Refining Graph Diffusion for Long-Term Memory in LLM Agents
item.description: ActionRAG replaces standard vector-based memory pipelines—which fragment entities during indexing and rely on static similarity scores for retrieval—with a graph architecture using tiered entity resolution and query-conditioned diffusion over a bounded local evidence graph. The implementation adds engineering complexity to construct and maintain the entity graph, though query-time synthesis remains under $0.001 and retrieval-side latency is approximately 441ms. Entity resolution can still incorrectly merge or split referents in the persistent store, and graph diffusion may propagate retrieval errors or fail to recover missing evidence if the local graph topology is sparse. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Sparse Bayesian Neural Networks via Sticky Piecewise Deterministic Markov Processes
item.description: This method replaces post-hoc pruning of dense networks with spike-and-slab priors and sticky PDMP samplers that set weights exactly to zero during posterior sampling. It costs substantial implementation complexity in constructing numerical rate bounds and PDMC samplers, with MCMC mixing and diagnostic overhead that likely exceeds standard training or HMC baselines. It can fail if rate bounds are incorrectly constructed or if posterior sampling fails to converge, yielding unreliable uncertainty estimates and sparse structures. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency
item.description: The method replaces repeated reasoning callbacks after tool feedback with guarded reuse of previously resolved decisions stored as Executable Decision Graphs, substituting certified callbacks through the native interface while actor weights remain fixed. It costs the engineering complexity of a controller at the model-tool boundary, RSI-based refinement of harness configurations with validation, and the infrastructure for storing graphs with literal arguments, causal dependencies, and guards. It can fail when new semantic decisions, unsupported evidence, or selector abstention force fallback to the original actor, and gains are benchmark-dependent on repeated-decision structure that production workloads may not exhibit. 0 independent implementations, 123 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: On the Limits of Sparse Linear Model with Shuffled Differential Privacy
item.description: The paper establishes theoretical lower and upper bounds for privately estimating sparse linear models under shuffled differential privacy, replacing local-DP or central-DP estimators in that statistical setting. It costs nothing to deploy because it contributes no production artifact: the interactive algorithm assumes a distributed user population each holding multiple samples under a shuffle trust model. It does not apply to typical ML engineering practice, and adopting its privacy accounting would fail any workload that lacks shuffled multi-user data collection. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Neural LoFi with Backward Coupling: A Spectral Theory of Cross-Layer Feature Learning
item.description: It replaces standard end-to-end backpropagation training (and the purely forward, layer-wise Neural LoFi surrogate) with a spectral layer-wise scheme in which upper-layer sensitivities generate sample-dependent effective labels for earlier layers. The cost is a substantially more complex training procedure—deriving cross-layer correlation operators, coupled modes, and continuous-time dynamics—plus custom implementation with no evidence of support for modern deep architectures. It can fail outside the analyzed small-initialization, smooth-activation, three-layer and hierarchical multi-index settings, and the only validation is binary CIFAR-10, so generalization to production tasks is unestablished. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Singular Geometry of Low-Rank Adaptation
item.description: The paper analyzes the singular statistical geometry of LoRA fine-tuning, characterizing learning complexity via the real log canonical threshold rather than parameter count, and proposes a curvature-corrected multi-temperature RLCT estimator; it replaces naive parameter-count complexity reasoning, not any standard production LoRA training procedure. The cost of adoption is additional mathematical machinery and diagnostics layered onto existing fine-tuning, with no demonstrated reduction in compute, memory, or latency. The analysis rests on local linearization and covariance nondegeneracy assumptions that can fail in practice, and the experiments are limited to MLP and small transformer settings rather than production-scale fine-tuning. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Sustainability of TSFM Deployment and Pretraining: From Carbon Footprint Analysis to Mitigation via Pruning
item.description: Replaces full Chronos-2 inference (and its amortized pretraining carbon cost) with a structurally pruned TSFM using a gradient-free criterion to drop one encoder block, versus supervised standalone models that need periodic retraining. Costs a 7.9% parameter reduction (6-9% FLOPs, CO2, and latency savings) with no retraining overhead, and requires choosing between TSFM and classical models based on deployment scale: classical remains cheaper indefinitely for small or rarely queried workloads. Can fail if the deployment is small or infrequently queried (pretraining never amortizes), if the gradient-free criterion underperforms on data outside the 25-task benchmark, or if undetected accuracy regressions appear on domain-specific series. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Do "True" and "False" Add Up to One? Complement Consistency in LLM-Agent Opinion Simulations
item.description: This is a validation procedure, not a component: it replaces the assumption that an agent's reported probability reflects a position on a claim by requiring the report on a claim and on its complement to sum to one, with an optional symmetrization step (averaging each answer with the complement of its paired answer) that doubles inference calls per state. Its cost is a parallel complementary-wording evaluation run and, if symmetrization is adopted in production, twice the sampling per reported probability, with no guarantee of improved accuracy since the symmetrized reports beat the better original wording at the final round for only one of three tested models. What can fail is precisely what the paper demonstrates in three small open models: paired reports exceed one on average, mirror populations diverge under feedback, and any downstream reading of simulated probabilities as beliefs can be invalid. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: LoCA: Enabling Multi-Modality in Geospatial Location Encoders
item.description: LoCA replaces direct contrastive training of a location encoder against a single frozen image encoder with a two-stage pipeline: first co-train Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 encoders into a high-rank co-aligned target, then train location and tabular encoders as frozen-backbone projection adapters. The cost is a supervised multimodal pretraining stage requiring paired SAR/optical imagery and adapter training, plus the proven intrinsic dimension ceiling of 2 that no architecture can remove. It can fail when paired multimodal imagery is unavailable, when frozen image encoders are mismatched to the target geography or downstream task, or when the location embedding's rank limitation binds on tasks needing fine spatial discrimination. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Learning Positive Linear Combinations of ReLUs in Fully Polynomial Time
item.description: This is a theoretical computer science paper establishing the first fully-polynomial time PAC learning algorithm for positive linear combinations of ReLUs under Gaussian inputs; it does not replace any practical production method. The 'cost' is purely theoretical sample and time complexity bounds (poly(d, k, 1/ε)), with no implementation, benchmarks, or engineering artifacts. The method is inapplicable to the reader's constrained infrastructure and production goals, as it addresses a fundamental learnability question rather than an engineering optimization. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Where Rounding Happens Matters: Rounding-Location Alignment Stabilizes LLM Reinforcement Learning
item.description: The method replaces full-stack inference/training alignment, global precision changes, or modified RL objectives with targeted FP32 retention of intermediates at three rounding locations (RoPE, SwiGLU, residual RMSNorm) in the training stack. It costs a modest increase in training-side memory for retained FP32 intermediates and requires implementation access to the training framework's forward pass; inference engine, kernels, and learning objective remain unchanged. It can fail if applied to architectures or frameworks where the dominant train-inference mismatch arises from other operators, and its findings are validated only on Qwen-family models, so transfer to other model families or RL setups is unverified. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
item.description: DexPort replaces full robot-arm teleoperation and human-motion retargeting with a portable interface built from the same dexterous hand used at deployment, recording commanded joint targets and measured states while the operator controls wrist motion and selects finger skills. The cost is specialized high-DoF robot-hand hardware, a skill set that must be designed per hand, and behavior-cloning training that requires thousands of demonstrations (over 2,500 collected here), plus a camera and compute for visuomotor policy training. Failure modes include operator skill-selection errors propagating into demonstrations, limited skill coverage for tasks outside the designed repertoire, and policies that inherit the hand's embodiment specificity so they do not transfer to other robot hands. 0 independent implementations, 218 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Hidden Cartographer: Hidden State Guided Data Selection for Dual Budgeted Instruction Tuning
item.description: It replaces pseudo-label-based selection and conventional active learning with a two-stage process: progressive candidate expansion using a hidden-state proxy, then exact training-dynamics pruning to a compact fine-tuning subset. It costs repeated proxy updates and training-dynamics recomputation during the expansion loop, adding pipeline complexity and compute beyond a single-pass selection, though it reduces annotation and fine-tuning volume substantially. It can fail if the proxy's hidden-state signals mischaracterize which examples are valuable, or if domain-specific dynamics do not transfer, making validation on the reader's own data distribution necessary before relying on the reported accuracy advantage. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Improving the Expressive Power of Hybrid Sequence Models via Multi-Hop Retrieval
item.description: MuRA replaces conventional hybrid blocks (full-attention layers plus fixed-state efficient layers) by letting efficient layers perform m sequential retrieval hops from a shared KV cache, which provably enables m-function composition where existing blocks require capacity scaling as Omega(sqrt(n)) even for two hops. The cost is architectural: it is a new block design that requires training from scratch or fine-tuning a custom implementation, with added implementation complexity in the retrieval mechanism, though it preserves asymptotic compute and memory efficiency. It can fail in practice because the evidence is a theoretical expressivity hierarchy plus synthetic composition tasks; there is no demonstration on pretrained models, real downstream benchmarks, or pretrained-checkpoint compatibility, so gains may not transfer to production workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: MOSAIC: Multi-Objective Search for Allocating Inference Cache Across LLM Decoder Layers
item.description: MOSAIC replaces uniform per-layer KV-cache budgets (as used by SnapKV, H2O, AdaKV, L2Norm-style eviction) with a per-layer budget allocation found by one multi-objective search whose best allocation transfers across target budgets, optionally refined by a budget-constrained search. The cost is a one-time offline search per model and eviction method (reported as cheaper than EvolKV, but still multi-evaluation GPU work on a single 24 GB card for 7-8B models), plus serving-side plumbing to track and enforce per-layer budgets, with no runtime quality loss claimed at matched budgets. It can fail if the searched allocation does not transfer to models, tasks, context lengths, or eviction methods outside the validated Llama-3-8B / Mistral-7B and RULER/LongBench settings, or if the serving stack cannot apply heterogeneous per-layer budgets without kernel or scheduler changes. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: System X: An LLM Decision Model That Replies from Its Own KV Cache
item.description: The method replaces a separate full-prompt second LLM call for text replies with continuation from the decision model's existing KV cache after a Jev-style option readout. It costs a LoRA fine-tuning pipeline, routing-data curation, and added serving complexity, and gains remain workload-dependent rather than a fixed multiplicative factor. Failures include state conflicts, unsupported reply details, possible instruction-following degradation from added support data, and reply-judge results confounded by prompt and generation-limit differences. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Reliability-Preserving Compression for Deployable Medical Image Segmentation
item.description: SGAV-MP replaces uniform post-training quantization, pruning, or distillation pipelines that select layer precisions by Dice and size alone, by scoring quantization actions on a benefit-risk basis and accepting them only after full-model reliability validation on a calibration set. The cost is an added calibration and validation stage per quantization candidate, plus reliance on a backend such as TensorRT to convert stored compression into actual runtime speedup, which the paper reports separately. It can fail if the calibration set is unrepresentative of deployment data, in which case the accepted precision assignments may preserve uncertainty agreement in validation but not in production, and the method is validated only on MRI/CT segmentation, so transfer to other tasks is unverified. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: StreamAhead: Real-Time Streaming Video Question Answering via Adaptive Precomputation
item.description: StreamAhead replaces the standard practice of building full KV caches for every incoming video segment with a tiered scheme that keeps segments at cheap representation levels (visual features) and materializes KV caches only for query-retrieved segments. The cost is an offline profiling step per segment and model, a runtime scheduler that pipelines segment computation across CPU and GPU concurrently with queries, and the query-time compute of completing KV caches for retrieved segments. It can fail when the retrieval stage selects the wrong segments, when query arrival bursts exceed the scheduler's ability to complete KV caches within latency targets, or when the offline cost profiles do not transfer to the deployment hardware or model. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Adversarial Post-Training of Foundation Models for High-Frequency Trading
item.description: The method replaces additional cross-entropy pre-training of a limit-order-book generator with a short adversarial post-training stage: a WGAN critic evaluates free-running rollouts through the real matching engine and evolution strategies update rank-4 LoRA perturbations under a KL trust region. It costs under 50M training tokens and roughly 12 GPU-hours per seed, but presupposes an existing pre-trained LOB foundation model (a 48B-token pre-training budget), access to a non-differentiable matching engine, and online critic infrastructure. It can fail through reward hacking of the critic, as the paper's own analysis notes, and its gains are specific to market-simulation fidelity rather than general language-model quality. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: LOOP: Recovery-Aligned Iterative Layer Pruning via On-Policy Distillation
item.description: Replaces one-shot layer pruning followed by a single recovery phase with an iterative loop that removes one layer at a time, runs short on-policy distillation after each removal, and reuses recovery signals to select subsequent layers. Costs repeated distillation cycles with on-policy trajectory generation (teacher rollouts at every shot), which raises compute and wall-clock budget well beyond a one-shot prune, though it preserves a dense architecture that runs on standard hardware after pruning. Can fail if the per-shot recovery budget is insufficient to make the pruning signal informative, if on-policy distillation is unstable for the target model, or if the accuracy gains over cheaper one-shot baselines do not justify the added training cost on a limited budget. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Corrected Block Sparse Spectral Optimization: Exact Models, Finite Identification, and Local Dynamics
item.description: Replaces dense PCA and the ambiguous standard block generalized-power sparse-PCA formulation with a primal-derived soft-threshold objective (A-SQ), a safeguarded Riemannian ascent with proven convergence, finite support identification, and post-identification refitting via power iteration. Cost is modest: Stiefel updates and thresholding on covariance-scale data run on a single GPU or CPU, with added implementation complexity for tie-breaking, zero-response columns, and mask-before-refit conventions. It can fail when the strict threshold-margin assumption does not hold, delaying or preventing support identification, and the quality gains are dataset-specific additive AMI improvements rather than guaranteed uplifts on arbitrary workloads. 1 independent implementation, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: How Much Does One Wrong Answer Cost? Error Propagation in Constraint Pruning with Noisy LLM Oracles
item.description: The method does not replace constraint pruning itself; it replaces the assumption that a correct oracle makes query order irrelevant, prescribing query orders (notably pivot orders for entity resolution) that bound how far one wrong LLM answer propagates. It costs nothing in extra queries or infrastructure, only deliberate ordering of the same yes/no questions, with pivot ordering being simple to implement. It can fail when error independence or small-epsilon assumptions break down (correlated oracle errors, systematic biases toward certain record pairs), since the guarantees are first-order in epsilon and the common most-similar-first ordering is provably the worst in one dimension. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: test.

item.title: The KV-Surgeon: Compensation-Aware Offline KV-Cache Compaction
item.description: Replaces per-entry independent scoring for KV-cache eviction (e.g., attention matching) with a calibration-data-driven quadratic surrogate that jointly selects removals and compensates remaining entries, accounting for softmax renormalization. Cost is a one-time offline compaction pass with calibration data per fixed context, plus the memory of retaining a small calibration set; the compacted cache then reduces per-query memory and compute on repeated queries. It can fail when the queried context is not fixed and reused (no amortization of the offline cost), when calibration data is unrepresentative of production queries, or when compaction ratios are pushed beyond the validated operating points. 2 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Latent Projection for Latent Planning
item.description: The method replaces the raw l2 distance between predicted and goal latents with an l2 distance restricted to the k-dimensional subspace that the learned state dynamics propagate with least uncertainty, derived from a normal-matrix transition model fit under SIGReg regularization. The cost is fitting a single constrained matrix A post hoc; the encoder, predictor, rollout, and planner remain unchanged, adding negligible compute. The approach can fail if the SIGReg and Gauss-Markov assumptions do not hold for the reader's environment, if the latent dynamics are not well-approximated by a normal linear map, and the reported gains are demonstrated only on 2D navigation tasks, so transfer to other domains is unvalidated. 1 independent implementation, 1 star. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ORBIT: Autoregressive Time Series Generation via Next Frequency-Band Prediction
item.description: ORBIT replaces conventional time-series generative models (GANs, diffusion models, and standard autoregressive transformers) with a two-stage framework: a Frequency-Hierarchical VQ-VAE that decomposes latent representations into frequency bands with residual quantization, and a Frequency-Band Autoregressive Transformer that generates from low to high frequencies. The abstract claims state-of-the-art overall performance and superior inference efficiency compared with advanced baselines, but provides no quantitative factor in the abstract itself; assessing actual compute and memory costs requires consulting the full paper.
